name: Charge of a title, and its discharge
summary: A proprietor charges land or a lease to secure a debt, and in due course the chargee discharges it. The two ends of the same relationship.
triggers: A lender is taking security over registered land or a lease
Or an existing charge is being redeemed and released

not_this_if.fact: The charge is being sold on to another lender
not_this_if.why: That is a transfer of charge, LRA 57.

not_this_if.fact: Only part of the security is being released
not_this_if.why: That is a partial discharge, LRA 59.

not_this_if.fact: The terms of an existing charge are changing
not_this_if.why: That is a memorandum of variation, LRA 56.

statutory_basis.quote: A proprietor may by an instrument, in the prescribed form, charge any land or lease to secure the payment of an existing, future or a contingent debt
statutory_basis.effect: A charge is made on the prescribed form, which is LRA 53.

statutory_basis.quote: The charge shall be completed by its registration as an encumbrance
statutory_basis.effect: An unregistered charge is not a completed charge. Until it is registered as an encumbrance and the chargee registered as its proprietor, the lender does not have what it thinks it has.

statutory_basis.quote: The Registrar shall not register a charge, unless a land rent clearance
statutory_basis.effect: A charge over leasehold needs the rent clearance certificate and the consent to charge before it registers. Freehold is excepted, as are a condominium unit, an office in a building and certain subleases under subsection (5A).

statutory_basis.quote: A charge shall have effect as a security only and shall not operate as a transfer
statutory_basis.effect: The chargee takes security, not ownership. This is worth saying to a client who thinks the bank now owns the land.

statutory_basis.quote: shall be obtained before the second or subsequent charge is created
statutory_basis.effect: The first chargee's consent must be obtained before the second charge is created, not after. Creating first and seeking consent afterwards is the wrong order and LRA 55 is the instrument.

statutory_basis.quote: An instrument required by law to be stamped shall not be accepted for registration unless it is stamped
statutory_basis.effect: Stamping gates registration of a charge as of a transfer.

statutory_basis.quote: is void for all purposes unless the land control board for the land control area or division in which the land is situated has given its consent in respect of that transaction in accordance with this Act
statutory_basis.effect: Agricultural land within a land control area cannot be dealt with without the board's consent. Registration does not cure the want of it.

statutory_basis.quote: within six months of the making of the agreement for the controlled transaction
statutory_basis.effect: The clock runs from the agreement, not from completion. Six months, extendable only by the High Court for sufficient reason.

bundle.role: Application for the consent of the land control board, in the prescribed form
bundle.condition: A charge is being created over agricultural land within a land control area. Not for a discharge alone.
bundle.why: Section 6(1) catches a mortgage or charge of agricultural land expressly.
Everything lodged goes under a general application.

bundle.role: Consent of the first chargee to a second or subsequent charge
bundle.condition: A charge already sits on the title and a further charge is being created
bundle.why: Section 57(2) requires the first chargee's consent before the second charge is created.

bundle.condition: An existing charge is being redeemed in full
bundle.why: The chargee releases the security. Note that a discharge is given by the chargee over the title, not to the purchaser.

drafted_together.why: A charge lodges under a general application like any other instrument.

consents.name: Consent of the first chargee
consents.when_required: A second or subsequent charge is being created
consents.deadline: Before the second charge is created
consents.consequence_if_missed: The consent is required before creation, so seeking it afterwards does not cure the sequence. LRA 55 is the form.

consents.name: Consent to charge, with a land rent clearance certificate
consents.when_not_required: The land is freehold, or the charge relates to a condominium unit, an office in a building, or certain subleases under s.56(5A)
consents.authority: The lessor, which for public land is the National Land Commission
consents.consequence_if_missed: The Registrar shall not register the charge.

consents.name: Land Control Board consent
consents.when_required: A charge is being created over agricultural land within a land control area
consents.authority: The land control board for the area
consents.consequence_if_missed: The charge is void for all purposes. A lender holding a void charge holds nothing.
consents.when_not_required: The land is not agricultural or lies outside a land control area; or the transaction is a discharge alone. Releasing a charge is not a controlled transaction.

clearances.name: Land rent clearance certificate
clearances.authority: the Ministry or the National Land Commission

sequence: Official search, to see what is already on the register.
If a charge already exists, obtain the first chargee's consent before creating the second one.
If a charge is being created, establish whether the land is agricultural and within a land control area. A discharge alone needs no Board consent.
On leasehold, obtain the consent to charge and the land rent clearance certificate.
Execute with verification, then lodge, and confirm the charge is registered as an encumbrance rather than assuming it.

traps.trap: Creating a second charge and then seeking the first chargee's consent
traps.why_wrong: Section 57(2) requires the consent before creation.

traps.trap: Treating an executed charge as security before it is registered
traps.why_wrong: Section 56(3) completes a charge by registration as an encumbrance. Until then the lender's position is not what it believes.

traps.trap: Describing a discharge as given in favour of the purchaser
traps.why_wrong: The chargee gives a discharge over the title. The purchaser is not the party discharging.

traps.trap: Forgetting that a charge of agricultural land is a controlled transaction
traps.why_wrong: Section 6(1) of the Land Control Act names mortgage and charge alongside sale. A void charge is worse for a lender than no charge.

practice_varies.step: Whether the charge and its stamping are presented together
practice_varies.note: Registries differ. Record what yours accepts.

verified_by.note: Bundles, sequence, alternatives and traps approved. Every statutory quote is proved against cached primary law by scripts/procedures/lint.js on each build; the readings remain ED's, approved by the advocate above. 2026-09-28: Robin confirmed that a discharge alone needs no Land Control Board consent; consent is scoped to creating a charge.
